government.note: Parliamentary constitutional monarchy with a ceremonial monarch. The Speaker of the Riksdag leads government formation, and a prime ministerial candidate takes office unless an absolute majority (175 of 349) votes against ('negative parliamentarism'). The 2003 euro referendum was non-binding and is the most recent national referendum.

system.note: Modified Sainte-Lague in 29 multi-member constituencies (310 seats) plus 39 national adjustment (levelling) seats. Parties need 4% nationally, or 12% in a constituency. seats_2000 is the 1998 election result; no mid-term changes before 1 January 2000 were checked.

start_2000.ideology_support_note: Derived from 1998 Riksdag vote shares (computed from the official vote counts): Social Democrats 36.4% (split 30.0 social democrat / 6.4 Third Way, a gameplay estimate), Moderates 22.9%, Left Party 12.0% plus small socialist and communist lists 0.1% (democratic socialist), Christian Democrats 11.7%, Centre Party 5.1% (agrarian), Liberal People's Party 4.7% (social liberal), Greens 4.5%, Sweden Democrats 0.4% and New Democracy 0.2% (right populist, rounded to 0.5%), Senior Citizen Interest Party 1.0% and other minor lists about 1.1% (big tent).
